1 euphemism

[ ˈyüfəˌmizəm ]
(n.) the substitution of an agreeable or inoffensive expression for one that may offend or suggest something unpleasant.

Cougar is the euphemism for a woman who has reached mid-life, who is single, financially secure and on the lookout for relationships with younger men—as in "prey."

item.title: W34 Tuesday
item.dc:creator: Samson Wang
item.description:
1 ostentatious

[ ˌästənˈtāshəs ]
(adj.) Ostentatious describes someone or something that displays wealth, knowledge, power, etc., in a way that is meant to attract attention, admiration, or envy. Things that are ostentatious tend to stand out as overly elaborate or conspicuous.

The resort town is famous for its extravagantly expensive summer homes, which some tourists view as impressive and others merely ostentatious.

item.title: W33 Tuseday
item.dc:creator: Samson Wang
item.description:
1 palatable

[ ˈpælətəbl ]
(adj.) (of food or drink) pleasant to taste.
This is a very palatable local red wine.

2 ounce

[ ouns ]
(n.) a unit of weight of one sixteenth of a pound avoirdupois (approximately 28 grams).
Melt three ounces of butter in a large frying pan.

3 naringin

[ nəˈrinjə̇n ]
柚苷，柚皮苷
(n.) Naringin is a flavonoid, specifically a flavanone glycoside, found in citrus fruits like grapefruit, and known for its bitter taste.

4 antioxidant

[ ˌæntiˈɒksɪdənt ]
(n.) a substance that inhibits oxidation, especially one used to counteract the deterioration of stored food products
An antioxidant is a substance that prevents or slow down oxidation, a chemical reaction that produces harmful free radicals.

5 arteriosclerosis

[ ɑ:ˌtɪəriəʊskləˈrəʊsɪs ]
(n.) Arteriosclerosis is a type of vascular disease where the blood vessels carrying oxygen away from the heart (arteries) become damaged from factors such as high cholesterol, high blood pressure, diabetes and certain genetic influences.

6 miniature

[ ˈmɪnətʃə(r) ]
(adj.) (especially of a replica of something) of a much smaller size than normal; very small.
Children dressed as miniature adults.

(n.) a thing that is much smaller than normal, especially a small replica or model.
Seven full-size car bodies and three miniatures were used.

(v.) represent on a smaller scale; reduce to miniature dimensions.
She saw her own reflection miniatured.

7 cleanse

[ klenz ]
(vt.) to rid of impurities by or as if by washing
It's that mystical state most athletes are lucky to achieve a few times in their careers. The mind is cleansed. The body is free.

8 citrus

[ ˈsi-trəs ]
(n.) any of a group of often thorny trees and shrubs (Citrus and related genera) of the rue family grown in warm regions for their edible fruit (such as the orange or lemon) with firm usually thick rind and pulpy flesh.
Go back in time and connect with nature at Neapolis Archeological Park, which has an ancient Greek theater, Roman amphitheater, and centuries-old citrus trees.

9 cruciferous

[ ˈkrüˈsif(ə)rəs ]
(adj.) any of a family (Brassicaceae synonym Cruciferae) of plants including the cabbage, turnip, and mustard
十字花科的
brussel sprout 芽球甘蓝

10 quinine

[ ˈkwīˌnīn ]
(n.) a salt of quinine used especially as an antipyretic, antimalarial, and bitter tonic
奎宁
Tonic water is sweetend soda that contains bitter-tasting chemcial compound called quinie.

（全文完）

item.title: Week33 Monday
item.dc:creator: Samson Wang
item.description:
1 ubiquitous

[ ju:ˈbɪkwɪtəs ]
(v.) - present everywhere
Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern society.

2 exacerbate

[ ɪgˈzæsəbeɪt ]
(v.) - to make a problem worse
Poor urban planing exacerbates traffic congestion.

3 ephemeral

[ ɪˈfemərəl ]
(adj.) - lasting for a very short time
Social media trends are often ephemeral.

4 pragmatic

[ prægˈmætɪk ]
(v.) - dealing with things sensibly and realistically
A pragmatic approach to education focus on practical skills.

5 resilient

[ rɪˈzɪliənt ]
(adj.) - able to recover from difficulties
Children are often more resilient than adults think.

6 detrimental

[ ˌdetrɪˈmentl ]
(adj.) - harmful or damaging
Lack of sleep can be detrimental to health.

7 inevitable

[ ɪnˈevɪtəbl ]
(adj.) - certain to happen, unavoidable
Technological advancement is inevitable in the 21st centuary.

8 conducive

[ kənˈdju:sɪv ]
(adj.) - making a certain situation likely or possible.
A quiet environment is conducive to effective studying.

9 paradigm

[ ˈpærədaɪm ]
(n.) - typical example or pattern
The internet caused a paradigm shift in communication.

10 precursor

[ pri:ˈkɜ:sə(r) ]
(n.) - something that comes before
The telegraph was a precursor to modern communications.

（全文完）

item.title: Week32 Friday
item.dc:creator: Samson Wang
item.description:
1 mitigate

[ ˈmɪtɪgeɪt ]
(v.) - make less severe
Planting trees helps mitigate the effects of climate change.

2 proliferation

[ prəˌlɪfəˈreɪʃn ]
(n.) - rapid increase
The proliferation of fast food has contributed to health problems.

3 precarious

[ prɪˈkeəriəs ]
(adj.) - dangerously unstable
Many workers face precarious employment conditions.

4 corroborate

[ kəˈrɒbəreɪt ]
(v.) - confirm with evidence
The witness testimony corroborated the defendant's story.

5 discretionary

[ dɪˈskreʃənəri ]
(adj.) - available for optional use
The company offers discretionary bonuses for exceptional work.

6 exemplary

[ ɪgˈzempləri ]
(adj.) - serving as a desirable model
The student showed exemplary behavior throughout the year.

7 facilitate

[ fəˈsɪlɪteɪt ]
(v.) - make easier
Technology facilitates global communication.

8 inconsequential

[ ɪnˌkɒnsɪˈkwenʃl ]
(adj.) - unimportant
The spelling mistake was inconsequential to the overall meaning.

9 novel

[ ˈnɒvl ]
(adj.) - new and original
The scientist proposed a novel approach to the problem.

10 stringent

[ ˈstrɪndʒənt ]
(adj.) - strict and precise
The university has stringent admission requirements.

（全文完）
